# Promoted to repo memory: drift-certification

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `drift-certification M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-07T09:01:04.464Z) — Statusline "staleness" is Claude Code's render cadence, not a sofar bug: `sofar statusline` is stateless (folds the log fresh, ~40ms), but Claude Code re-runs the statusLine command ONLY on session start, a new assistant message, /compact, permission-mode change, vim-mode toggle, or an optional `refreshInterval` timer (300ms debounce) — so an idle session's line freezes while another session advances the record. Fix is settings-side: add `"refreshInterval": <seconds>` to the statusLine entry. Two product gaps that follow: (1) STATUSLINE_SETTINGS_ENTRY (cli/init.ts) writes no refreshInterval; (2) isSofarStatusline() requires exactly 2 keys, so a user-added refreshInterval makes `statusline --uninstall` report "foreign" and refuse to remove it. Separately by design: an already-open session keeps the initiative its session_started registered (resolveSessionFirst/homeInitiative), so a branch rebind or a newly opened initiative never moves an old session's line — that half is intended, not stale.
- **M2** (2026-08-07T09:01:39.844Z) — Bench runner availability on this machine (established 2026-08-07 with the run owner): Claude Code is the ONLY scriptable-headless resume runner — arms are model tiers within one family (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001), never cross-vendor. codex/gpt-5.5 runs headless for GRADING only (isolated CODEX_HOME, wiring proven in scenario 2's Grader C), which is what keeps METHODOLOGY §7.4's cross-family grader requirement satisfiable. Cross-vendor RESUMPTION is manual (Codex Desktop / Cursor, run owner drives) and therefore small-n and never pooled into a scripted run's denominator. Consequence for any future bench claim: "across models" from a scripted run means across Claude tiers unless a manual arm is cited with its own n and bound.
- **M3** (2026-08-07T09:30:39.988Z) — Trap-corpus supply law (measured 2026-08-07 over 223 real decisions): a WELL-KEPT record is poor trap material. Decisions get echoed into goal lines, repo memory, session summaries, docs/SPEC prose, and above all code comments — doctor.ts:68-71 restates its own decision verbatim — so the decision entry is rarely the only carrier, and a session that complies may be copying the code in front of it rather than reading the record. Measured attrition on this corpus: 223 decisions -> 153 after mechanical screens -> 36 after leak+code-embodiment. Budget roughly 15-20% of a mature record's decisions as usable trap candidates before the temptation floor takes its cut, and plan trap-hungry benchmarks across SEVERAL repos from the start rather than expecting one record to supply them.
- **M4** (2026-08-07T10:42:16.050Z) — Headless bench-runner gotchas (found smoking the scenario-3 runner, 2026-08-07): (1) `claude -p` with a trailing positional prompt AFTER a variadic option silently loses it — `--disallowedTools Write Edit ...` swallows the prompt and claude exits 1 with "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument"; put the prompt immediately after -p. (2) A record's snapshot is NOT the commit at the decision's timestamp — sessions log decisions mid-flight and the record is committed afterwards, so that commit usually predates the record's existence; resolve with `git log --reverse -S<event_id> -- <record path>` to get the commit that introduced the event. (3) `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` plus disallowed edit tools is NOT read-only: the session still writes through Bash, so measure the footprint with a before/after tree walk — `git status` misses it twice over (it reports the builder's own writes to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md from `sofar init`, and is blind to gitignored dirs where artifacts often land).
- **M5** (2026-08-09T11:20:22.627Z) — Scenario-3 cost basis, measured 2026-08-09 (opus-5 list: $5/$25 per MTok, cache write 1.25x, read 0.1x). ONE P-cell probe session = $5.31-$32.32, n=4, mean $13.35. Cost is dominated by cache_read (49.8M tokens = $24.88 of the $32.32 outlier), which scales with turn count: these sessions genuinely build the feature (243 assistant turns / 136 tool calls on the expensive one). Cost therefore tracks REPO WEIGHT, not trap difficulty: brillo (large Next.js app) $32.32/28min; algrowth $5.31-$8.06/9-10min. Repo-weighted floor estimate over the frozen 20-trap set (brillo 7, algrowth 5, sofar-cloud 4, s2bench 3, sofar 1) = ~$357 per rep-round, so k=4 floor ~= $1,429 -- NOT the $2,586 a single brillo session extrapolates to. Certified run at 3 arms (sonnet ~0.6x opus list, haiku ~0.2x) ~= $643 per R-round, ~$900 with the 8 RG variants. Recompute from runs/*/*/*/meta.json rather than re-deriving: every meta carries per-turn usage.
- **M6** (2026-08-09T13:17:16.218Z) — Lever 1 (block Bash in the probe) does NOT cut scenario-3 cost — measured 2026-08-09 over the 5 completed non-attempt probe sessions (218 Bash calls, runs/**/turn*.stream.jsonl). Tool mix: 72.5% read/inspect (cat/grep/ls/find/head/wc/jq), 10.6% bare `cd`, 3.7% git read — i.e. 86.8% of Bash is navigation and reading that Read/Grep/Glob do equally well. Only 6.0% is genuine execution (build/test 2.8%, curl/dev-server 1.8%, mkdir/write 1.4%). Result weight per call: Bash averages 1,395 chars, Read averages 7,542 chars — 5.4x heavier. So denying Bash redirects ~87% of those calls into a MORE context-expensive tool while removing only the ~6% execution tail; since cache_read scales with turn count x context size, expected saving is small and plausibly negative, not the order of magnitude the SCALE REVIEW note assumed. The note's cost premise for lever 1 is therefore unsupported; its realism cost (probe understating the execution rate, TRAP-SPEC 3.4) is real either way. Recompute this mix from the streams rather than re-deriving: map tool_use ids to tool_result payload sizes.
- **M7** (2026-08-09T14:11:22.562Z) — Cloning a cell with `--single-branch` is NOT enough to make it recovery-proof — `git clone` copies TAGS regardless, and a tag pointing at or after the snapshot keeps the pre-doctor commit reachable, so `git show <tag>:.sofar/...` hands back the undoctored record. It hides from both `git branch` (tags are not branches) and `git fsck --unreachable` (a tag is a perfectly good ref, so nothing is unreachable). Found 2026-08-09 when verify_recovery_proof failed on sofar-cloud-mac-app-D5, whose host carries desktop-v0.1.0..v0.3.1; the sofar host has no tags, which is why the first cell verified clean and the hole survived one round of checking. Fix: clone with `--no-tags`, and assert over `git for-each-ref` (every ref) rather than `git branch`. General lesson for any bench that doctors a repo: enumerate refs, never branches.
